items.grounds: Re-swept at skeleton tier, verse counts, each object named. The pair הַגִּ֣ידוּ וְהַגִּ֔ישׁוּ (oshb:Isa.45.21, byte tier; tokens 1-2 of 23) stands in 1 verse book-wide, Isa.45.21. The second member וְהַגִּ֔ישׁוּ (oshb:Isa.45.21, byte tier) alone: 1 verse; without its vav the same skeleton also reaches הַגִּ֨ישׁוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.41.21, byte tier), 2 verses. The first member הַגִּ֣ידוּ (oshb:Isa.45.21, byte tier) alone: 6 verses, Isa.3.9, Isa.41.22, Isa.41.23, Isa.45.21, Isa.48.20, Isa.66.19, exactly the row's digit, and that 6 is itself blended across form classes, argued from the pointing since the staged extract carries no morphology layer: verse-initial imperatives at 41:23 and 45:21, verse-medial imperatives הַגִּ֜ידוּ (oshb:Isa.41.22, byte tier; token 10 of 17) and הַגִּ֤ידוּ (oshb:Isa.48.20, byte tier; token 7 of 18), and hiriq-pointed suffix-conjugation forms הִגִּ֖ידוּ (oshb:Isa.3.9, byte tier; token 7 of 15) and וְהִגִּ֥ידוּ (oshb:Isa.66.19, byte tier; token 27 of 30). The sentence names the imperative pair and counts the single declare-token's skeleton across all its forms: a blended count object carrying a defective digit. Not load-bearing: the front seam rests on הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וָבֹ֛אוּ הִֽתְנַגְּשׁ֥וּ יַחְדָּ֖ו פְּלִיטֵ֣י הַגּוֹיִ֑ם (oshb:Isa.45.20, byte tier), which re-collates. Confirm at medium.

MT 41:22 (17 tokens) opens יַגִּ֨ישׁוּ֙ וְיַגִּ֣ידוּ (oshb:Isa.41.22, byte tier; tokens 1-2), the same two roots as the row's pair but yod-initial prefix-conjugation forms in reversed order, so its skeleton is not the pair's skeleton; the verse's only patah-pointed imperative הַגִּ֜ידוּ (oshb:Isa.41.22, byte tier) is token 10 of 17 (the finding says token 9; verse-medial either way). MT 41:23 (14 tokens) opens הַגִּ֨ידוּ֙ הָאֹתִיּ֣וֹת (oshb:Isa.41.23, byte tier) and carries no token of the second member's skeleton: the vav-bearing member וְהַגִּ֔ישׁוּ (oshb:Isa.45.21, byte tier) sweeps 1 verse and the pair הַגִּ֣ידוּ וְהַגִּ֔ישׁוּ (oshb:Isa.45.21, byte tier) sweeps 1 verse, both Isa.45.21 only (skeleton tier, verse counts). The row's 'skeleton matches the same imperative pair opening ... Isa.41.22 and Isa.41.23' is therefore false at skeleton tier for both verses; what survives is a single declare-imperative shared at skeleton tier, verse-initial at 41:23 only, plus a root-level, reversed, non-imperative echo at 41:22 that an honest restatement may name as such. Not load-bearing: the seam driver הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וָבֹ֛אוּ הִֽתְנַגְּשׁ֥וּ יַחְדָּ֖ו פְּלִיטֵ֣י הַגּוֹיִ֑ם (oshb:Isa.45.20, byte tier) stands. Confirm at medium.

MT 46:1 has 12 tokens: it opens כָּרַ֥ע בֵּל֙ קֹרֵ֣ס נְב֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier; tokens 1-4, suffix-conjugation verbs each with a freshly named subject), and the burden noun מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier) is tokens 11-12 of 12, verse-final (the finding's 'tokens 10-11' is off by one; the position the row asserts is false either way). The noun's bytes מַשָּׂ֖א (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier) are byte-identical to the 10 verse-initial massa headers (byte sweep: 11 verses, the 10 header sites plus 46:1), so verse position is the only discriminator between header-massa and burden-massa at this site, the very datum the sentence misstates. Marks (single witness): PE at oshb:Isa.45.17, no PE or SAMEKH at MT 45:18-46:1, SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.46.2; none at this seam, absence being no counterevidence, and the row claims none. The row's only back-seam warrant hangs a byte-true substance (a different subject opens at 46:1) on a byte-false position; the seam survives on the subject change, so this is a defective warrant, not a boundary defect. Confirm at medium.

The row's 46:1 splices are נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם עֲמוּס֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier; tokens 9-10 of 12) and מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier; tokens 11-12 of 12); the finding's 'only Hebrew spliced' undercounts by one run, but neither run is the onset. The verse-initial onset כָּרַ֥ע בֵּל֙ קֹרֵ֣ס נְב֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier; tokens 1-4, two suffix-conjugation verbs each with a freshly named subject, the explicit scene shift) is never spliced, so the front-seam warrant rides on the WEB quotation alone. Isa.45.25 appears in neither the prose nor boundary_evidence_refs (verified against the shipped list), leaving the preceding close בַּיהוָ֛ה יִצְדְּק֥וּ וְיִֽתְהַלְל֖וּ כָּל זֶ֥רַע יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.45.25, byte tier) uncharacterised. Marks (single witness): PE at oshb:Isa.45.17, none at MT 45:18-46:1, SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.46.2; no mark at this seam, absence not counterevidence. The seam is sound on the onset bytes, so the defect is a byte-unengaged, one-edged warrant rather than a boundary defect; the pointed-splice mandate for boundary-relevant claims makes it more than a mechanical shortfall. Confirm at medium.

Per attested spelling, skeleton tier, verse counts: נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier) 1 verse; עֲמוּס֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier) 1; הַֽעֲמֻסִים֙ (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte tier) 1; הַנְּשֻׂאִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte tier) 3, Isa.2.13, Isa.45.20, Isa.46.3, where the 45:20 site is הַנֹּֽשְׂאִים֙ (oshb:Isa.45.20, byte tier; token 9 of 17, an active-sense participle inside the preceding row's span) and 2:13 is וְהַנִּשָּׂאִ֑ים (oshb:Isa.2.13, byte tier), a differently pointed participle of the same skeleton. The row's 'plene and defective spellings each standing in exactly 1 verse' is true only if its object is the vav-plene/defective pair on the second root, עֲמוּס֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier) against הַֽעֲמֻסִים֙ (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte tier); placed directly after four cited forms the sentence never says so, and under the four-form reading it is false by a factor of three, with the undisclosed recurrence sitting just across the row's own front seam at 45:20 (a skeleton-tier straddle with different pointing, not byte-true, so it argues for disclosure, not restructuring). Re-verified true: the burden noun's accents differ, U+0596 tipcha in מַשָּׂ֖א (oshb:Isa.46.1, byte tier) against U+0591 etnachta in מַשָּׂ֑א (oshb:Isa.46.2, byte tier), equal at accent-stripped tier; and the rescue-root skeleton of וַאֲמַלֵּֽט (oshb:Isa.46.4, byte tier) sweeps 7 verses book-wide (Isa.20.6, 34.15, 37.38, 46.2, 46.4, 49.24, 49.25). An unnamed count object with a false available reading is a defective digit claim; not load-bearing, since the row itself declines the device as a driver. Confirm at medium.

Re-collated: שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֖י אַבִּ֣ירֵי לֵ֑ב (oshb:Isa.46.12, byte tier; tokens 1-4 of 6) against שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte tier; tokens 1-4 of 14). The summons שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ (oshb:Isa.46.3, byte tier) recurs at byte tier only at Isa.51.7, while at accent-stripped tier it stands in 4 verses (Isa.46.3, 46.12, 51.1, 51.7): the row's two summonses match at accent-stripped tier and differ at byte tier, as the row says. Marks (single witness): SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.46.11 (a K/Q-bearing verse) and SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.46.7, so both candidate cuts sit after a mark and the tier-3 layer does not discriminate. The 46:12 onset is a verse-initial repeated summons plus a new plural vocative, the same signal class the row drives its own front seam on at 46:3 and the following row drives at רְדִ֣י וּשְׁבִ֣י (oshb:Isa.47.1, byte tier); the 46:8 onset זִכְרוּ זֹ֖את (oshb:Isa.46.8, byte tier) with פוֹשְׁעִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.46.8, byte tier; token 5 of 7, a plural addressee in WEB) is an imperative onset too but lacks the repeated formula, and the row itself reports no onset there. So strongest_rejected_alternative names the rival the row's own prose rates weaker and omits the one it concedes: a mandated-field disclosure defect. The bracket-closing ground is argued from bytes and stays a legitimate reading, so the boundary is not impugned here (span_change false); the finding's 48:1 addressee claim lies outside this slice, unverified, and nothing turns on it. Confirm at medium.

Bytes: the span opens וַתֹּ֥אמֶר צִיּ֖וֹן (oshb:Isa.49.14, byte tier); MT 49:15 (12 tokens) opens הֲתִשְׁכַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ עוּלָ֔הּ (oshb:Isa.49.15, byte tier), a prefix-conjugation third-feminine form with an indefinite subject, and its only second-person element is the closing 2fs suffix of אֶשְׁכָּחֵֽךְ (oshb:Isa.49.15, byte tier; token 12), argued from the pointing (no morphology layer). Digits re-swept clean: the forget-root skeleton stands in 9 verses book-wide with exactly 2 in ch 49, Isa.49.14 and Isa.49.15 (skeleton tier, verse counts); SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.49.13 present (single witness; the verse is also K/Q-bearing). Against the finding: the two fields reconcile on these bytes. The rationale characterises the verse's onset form (third person: true); the rejected-alternative characterises the address mode of the unit beginning there (second person: true, the following row's seven per-verse 2fs tokens all re-collate at byte tier, its 49:15 token being this same suffix); the next row's 'second-person answer opens at 49:15' is that unit-level claim, not a contrary reading of the onset. No byte-false statement is present and the seam ground (speaker change on the narrated attribution formula) is sound, so 'incompatible' overstates. Against the row: its alternative field leans on 'second-person' exactly where its rationale denies a second-person opening and supplies no reconciling scope note, so a reader is left with two apparent seam signals in one row: a precision/disclosure shortfall in a mandated field, not a defective warrant. Downgrade to low.

Re-derived from bytes: the front seam carries the divine messenger frame כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.50.1, byte tier; tokens 1-3 of 23, divine-frame class, not the chs 36-37 royal-messenger class), the back seam the fronted title with a first-person recipient אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה נָ֤תַן לִי֙ (oshb:Isa.50.4, byte tier; tokens 1-4 of 19); marks (single witness): SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.49.26 and oshb:Isa.50.3, PE at oshb:Isa.50.11, paseq segs at MT 50:1 and 50:4 (count-only). Both seams are tier-1 sound, as the finding says. The shipped strongest_rejected_alternative weighs only the unit_type tag ('Tagging this span salvation_oracle ... was considered and set aside ...', verified verbatim) and no rival span, merge or split is tested in any field; the four neighbouring rows visible in this slice each name a rival span, so the finding's batch-wide claim holds for every row I can see (the full batch is outside this slice). The field's mandated function, rival cuts disclosed, goes undischarged: a defective warrant component rather than a boundary defect, and an absent rival is no lesser shortfall than a mis-named one, so medium is the right tier. Confirm at medium.
